title: Israel Is Attacking Wikipedia
excerpt: Read our new report: twenty years of documented attacks on Wikipedia, and what this means for the information you get from search and AI.
content_html:
1. 01

    from pro-Israel PACs to 26 U.S. politicians behind it

    The US government used a report from the ADL to attack Wikipedia. The goal is for the Israel Lobby to gain influence over it.

    Read more: Section 4
  2. 02

    Israel’s 2026 propaganda budget, up from $150M

    Wikipedia feeds Google Search and every major AI chatbot. Israel’s 2026 propaganda budget is $729M, up from $150M in 2025. That includes a $46.5M contract to make AI chatbots more pro-Israel.

    Read more: Section 2.2
  3. 03

    Our research shows that the ADL's partner in the attack on Wikipedia was likely funded by billionaire tech bros. “Builders for Tomorrow” came out of “Builders for Israel”, a WhatsApp group started in 2023 with Sheryl Sandberg, Bill Ackman, Shaun Maguire, and David Marcus.

    Read more: Section 4.6.2
  4. 04

    From the ADL’s mouth: “The pressure came from several directions: congressional scrutiny, including a House Committee on Oversight investigation and a bipartisan Congressional letter from 23 members, federal inquiries from the Department of Justice and the Senate Commerce Committee; enforcement work by Wikipedia’s NPOV-policy editors, ADL reporting, and broader media scrutiny.”

    Read more: Section 6.5.2.1
  5. 05

    ADL claims that survived scrutiny

    We checked every claim in the ADL’s “Editing for Hate” report, and the “Damage Done”. No claim survived scrutiny. It doesn’t show a single false fact, or any antisemitic content added to Wikipedia.

    Read more: Section 6
  6. 06

    Prize from an Israeli foundation, the largest prize he has received

    Wikipedia founder Jimmy Wales calls himself a “strong supporter of Israel”, and has visited Israel over ten times. In 2025 he tried to influence the Gaza Genocide page to be more pro-Israel, in a clear abuse of power. In November 2026, he's trying again, with the Zionism page. We recommend that Wales step down from the Board and disable his user account

    Read more: Section 3.16
  7. 07

    civil rights groups who say #DropTheADL

  8. 08

    efforts since 2001, nine still active

    We document 17 pro-Israel efforts to manipulate Wikipedia since 2001. Nine are still active! From CAMERA’s secret editor recruitment to a “Wikipedia war room” and editing courses run by Zionist groups.

    Read more: Section 3
  9. 09

    full-time ADL analysts “tracking” Wikipedia editors

    Four groups are targeting Wikipedia editors: the Heritage Foundation, the ADL, NPOV and Builders for Tomorrow. Some editors who were doxxed have received death threats. The ADL’s CEO says he has 45 full-time analysts “tracking” Wikipedia editors, whom he calls “weirdos with email addresses”.

    Read more: Section 4.6
  10. 10

    is fewer edits than one experienced editor does in a day

    The ADL blamed a “systematic” coordinated editing campaign on us, then tried to launder their claims. But the ADL’s own data shows only 260 edits over 8 months, none of them in the core Palestine–Israel articles. That’s one fewer edit than the ADL’s own 2021 editing campaign.

    Read more: Section 6.6
  11. 11

    Look it up

    The ADL made a series of claims about Arabic Wikipedia, based on bad English translations, with no cultural context or understanding. Not surprisingly, they got it all wrong

    Read more: Section 6.4

Read the full report online Download PDF (7.0 MB)

This report started in March 2025, when the ADL published “Editing for Hate”. The report claims Wikipedia editors colluded to add antisemitism. US politicians started using it to attack Wikipedia. We wanted to know if the report itself was part of an influence operation.

We worked on three tracks:

  • Israel’s efforts to influence Wikipedia. We collected 17 publicly known campaigns from public reports, at least 9 of them still active. This is the first time they are documented in one place. (Sections 3 and 4)
  • The ADL report. We went through every claim and traced each one back to the Wikipedia edits and sources it cites. None held up. (Section 6)
  • The propaganda tools behind the attack. (Sections 2 and 5)

The ADL analysed Arabic Wikipedia through English translations. We went back to the original Arabic. (Section 6.4)

Links to Wikipedia are permalinks to the exact edit. Content from pro-Israel organisations and paywalled sources is linked through archive.org, so it can’t be removed or changed. (Appendix B)

Where we used AI for research, we name the tool and the prompts and publish the full conversation. AI-reconstructed links used in the report were checked by hand. (Appendices C, D and E)

Every claim in this report is footnoted, more than 500 in total.

This is a living document. We update it when corrections or new information come in. Found an error? Email contact@techforpalestine.org.

Tech for Palestine is a member-driven organization that brings together people, skills and resources. Through technology and collaboration, our members build tools and solutions that support the movement for Palestine.

These projects include: protest apps, tools for boycotting, support for Palestinian students & businesses, ethical tech alternatives, and many more.
